title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: Braised lamb mince under a fluffy mashed potato crust
excerpt: Slow-cooked lamb mince with vegetables and herbs in a rich, herby sauce, topped with a layer of golden, buttery mashed potato. The lamb version of the great British mince pie.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shepherd's pie is the lamb counterpart to cottage pie: the name refers to sheep farmers (shepherds) and the use of lamb mince rather than beef mince. The dish follows the same principle as cottage pie: braised mince under a mashed potato crust baked until golden. Shepherd's pie is associated with the tradition of using leftover cooked lamb from a Sunday roast, minced or finely chopped, to make a meal on Monday. The dish is often considered the most British of all British dishes alongside roast beef and fish and chips. Rosemary is the classical herb pairing with lamb; it is used in preference to thyme which is more suited to the beef version. The dish is considered by many British cooks to be comfort food in its most essential form: starchy, savoury, warm, and completely undemanding. The filling can be made up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated before topping and baking.

recipeTools.notes: A deep baking dish, approximately 30 x 20 cm.
A large saucepan for the filling and a separate saucepan for the mash.

content.text: Lamb mince has a higher fat content than beef mince. After browning, tip the mince into a colander briefly to drain some of the excess fat before continuing with the recipe: too much fat in the filling makes the pie greasy. The filling can be made a day ahead; stored cold in the fridge, a cold filling is actually easier to top with mash because it does not slide around under the potato. Top from cold, then bake as directed.

Brown the lamb mince in batches over high heat without stirring until deeply coloured. Drain briefly in a colander. In the same pan, soften the onion and carrot in any remaining fat over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato puree, and rosemary. Cook for 1 minute. Return the mince.

Add the wine and bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay. Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until thick and coating. Stir in the peas. Season. Transfer to a baking dish.

Boil the potatoes until tender, drain well, and mash with butter and warm milk. Season. Spread over the filling and drag a fork across the surface in ridges. Bake at 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6 for 25 to 30 minutes until golden. Serve from the dish.
